raw_response:
I am 60 years old, and I have farmed these same 3 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on the fertilizer bags and understand what the input dealer in town tells me, but I still trust my own eyes and what Lao Zhang does across the road more than any outside expert. Last year my wheat made about 500 kg per mu and my maize made about 600 kg per mu. This year I will do almost exactly the same thing, because change is risky, fertilizer prices have gone up again, and every bag I buy is real money out of my pocket. My wife and I do all the labor ourselves — 3 mu is just enough that we do not need to hire anyone, but it also means we cannot afford a bad harvest.

For my winter wheat: After the maize comes off in autumn, I will rotary till the ground with my small tiller and sow the improved wheat variety I bought from the dealer — the same one Lao Zhang planted last year and had good luck with. At sowing, I spread 80 jin per mu of compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind. That is 40 kg per mu, giving me about 6 kg each of nitrogen, phosphate, and potash. Then in spring, when the wheat turns green, I broadcast 20 jin of urea per mu, and another 20 jin at the jointing stage. Each 20 jin is 10 kg, and urea is 46% nitrogen, so that is about 4.6 kg nitrogen each time. Add the 6 kg from the compound, and I am at about 15 kg nitrogen per mu total. I know that is a little more than the poster at the agro-shop says, but last year I did the same and got 520 kg per mu. Better to waste a little fertilizer than to lose grain. I will irrigate three times: the overwintering water, the jointing water, and one at filling time. The well pump costs electricity, but if the wheat dries out at filling, the whole year is lost. I spray herbicide once in early spring, and if I see aphids or rust, I spray one more time — two pesticide applications in total.

For my summer maize: Right after wheat harvest in early June, I rotary till quick and plant hybrid maize seed. You cannot grow maize without hybrid seed now; the old varieties are gone. At planting, I put 60 jin per mu of compound fertilizer in the row — that is 30 kg of 15-15-15, giving me about 4.5 kg each of nitrogen, phosphate, and potash. When the maize hits the big trumpet stage, I side-dress 50 jin of urea per mu — 25 kg, which is about 11.5 kg nitrogen. Total nitrogen is about 16 kg per mu. I irrigate twice: once at jointing if the sky does not give rain, and once at filling. I do one herbicide spray after sowing, and one insecticide spray when the corn borers come, usually around tasseling — two pesticide applications. I expect 600 kg per mu if the weather holds.

I think about my whole budget. Spending more on fertilizer means less left for medicine or repairs, but a bad harvest is a disaster. I watch what my neighbors do. If Lao Zhang puts down a certain amount, I do something similar. That is how I have stayed alive on 3 mu for 40 years.
